title: What Does Salary Packaging Mean? A Guide to Hourly to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Understand what does salary packaging mean and how to convert hourly rates to annual salary for a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, with super paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to annual salary for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, $30/hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. Your fortnightly pay is weekly pay ($1,140) times two = $2,280 before tax and super. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or salary packaging.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44/hour for a 38-hour week. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries and occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Your actual pay may be above either if your employer offers more.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied and is super paid on top?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, a $30 base rate becomes $37.50 with loading. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (up to the $270,830 contribution base). Casual loading does not affect super calculations.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you are wondering **what does salary packaging mean**, it is a way to structure your pay with non-cash benefits, but for now let us focus on the basics: turning an hourly rate into an annual salary. The standard formula for a full-time worker is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a 38-hour week because that is the ordinary full-time hours used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two — useful for budgeting or comparing to salary offers.

### Example Calculation

Take an hourly rate of $35.00:
- Weekly gross: $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly gross: $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual gross: $1,330.00 × 52 = $69,160.00

This is before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base rate and optionally add 25% casual loading — do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Understanding Minimum and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get an extra 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum. The Fair Work Commission sets award rates, and you can find your specific pay guide via the [pay guides](/blog) page. These are industry or occupation averages, not a median for your exact job.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual loading (25%) is paid on top of your base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top by your employer, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For example, on a $30 base rate:
- Casual rate: $30 + 25% = $37.50/hour
- Super: 12% of $30 (not the casual rate) = $3.60/hour, paid separately

This is explained further on the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not confirmed here). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help estimate your net pay.

### Example Tax on $69,160 Annual Gross

- Tax-free threshold: $18,200
- Tax on next $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) at 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $24,160 ($45,001–$69,160) at 30% = $7,248
- Total tax: $11,268
- Medicare levy (2% of $69,160) = $1,383.20
- Net annual: $69,160 – $11,268 – $1,383.20 = $56,508.80

This is an estimate. It does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## What Does Salary Packaging Mean?

**What does salary packaging mean** in practice? It is an arrangement where you sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This can reduce your taxable income, but it affects your super guarantee base and may have fringe benefits tax implications. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page covers this in more detail. Remember, the annual pay estimate here assumes no salary sacrifice.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Using the $35/hour example:
- Fortnightly gross: $2,660
- Estimated tax per fortnight: roughly $433 (based on annual tax divided by 26)
- Medicare levy: about $53
- Net fortnightly: around $2,174

Super is paid on top quarterly or monthly, not in your regular pay. The [reference tables](/data) provide more breakdowns.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details on average earnings, see the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for full-time adult ordinary time is $2,083.70 per week, but that is an average across all industries, not a median for your specific role.
